title: Strict local dimension drop in a nowhere dense closed fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $t\in T$. Suppose the inverse image of $i(Z)$ in the ordinary fibre $X_t$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has empty interior. For every $z\in Z$ with $(f\circ i)(z)=t$, the local topological dimension [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] of $Z_t$ at $z$ is strictly smaller than the local topological dimension of $X_t$ at $i(z)$.

source.place: Tag 054X, final dimension contradiction; Tag 00OT (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-over-field) and Tag 00OS, local dimension and finite type domain dimension.

proof.text: Base-change the closed immersion i to the fibre at s = f(i(z)) = t. Construct the fibre map j with pullback.map and its pullback square. IsClosedImmersion is stable under this pullback, Scheme.Pullback.range_map identifies its range with the inverse image of i(Z), and injectivity of the ambient fibre inclusion identifies j((i composed with f).asFiber z) with f.asFiber(i z). These identifications are proved in Lean in the main theorem.

A point of a noetherian quasi-sober space specializes from the generic point of its irreducible component. If that generic point lies in a closed subset W, its whole component lies in W. NoetherianSpace.exists_isOpen_nonempty_subset_irreducibleComponent supplies a nonempty ambient open in the component, contradicting interior W = empty. The private proved helper exists_generalization_outside_closed carries out this argument.

Apply the source-library theorem topologicalKrullDim_lt_of_forall_exists_specializes with Z the whole space: a chain in W extends by an outside generalization. Thus dim B < n+1 implies dim W < n. The private proved helper closed_nowhere_dense_dimension_lt assembles this specialization and the subspace bound for the whole-space subtype.

For a closed embedding j:A into B with nowhere dense range, noetherian sober T0 target B and finite dim B, the local dimension at j(a) is neither bottom (every neighbourhood contains a) nor top (it is bounded by dim B), so equals a natural n. The iInf_lt_iff characterization supplies an open neighbourhood U containing j(a) with dim U < n+1. Restrict j to its inverse image V of U. The restricted map is an embedding with closed range, and its range is nowhere dense by the interior-preimage formula for the open subtype inclusion. The preceding chain-extension bound gives dim V = dim range(j restricted) < n; the infimum defining dim_a A is bounded by dim V. This proves the private helper local_dimension_lt_of_closed_embedding without using the affine component formula.

The ambient fibre is compact by quasi-compactness of f and locally of finite type over the residue field by base change. Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian and IsNoetherian.noetherianSpace give a noetherian target; schemes are sober T0. The proved source-library theorem topologicalKrullDim_ne_top_of_compactSpace gives finite dimension. Apply the private local-dimension helper to the fibre map j and rewrite the point identification from step 1.

lean.statement:
theorem fibre_dimension_lt_of_closed_interior_eq_empty
    {Z X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (t : T)
    (h : interior ((f.fiberι t) ⁻¹' Set.range i) = ∅)
    (z : Z) (hz : (i ≫ f) z = t) :
    topologicalKrullDimAt ((i ≫ f).asFiber z) <
      topologicalKrullDimAt (f.asFiber (i z))
